worksheet.title: The Extra Block
worksheet.subtitle: Take out the block that goes too far
worksheet.learning_goal: I can fix a program by removing an extra block.

parts.title: Too far!
parts.text: Sometimes a program has one EXTRA block, so Bit goes too far and overshoots the target. Run the code, find the extra block, and cross it out to fix the program.

parts.title: Run it — too far
parts.prompt: Run Program 1 from 1. What number does Bit land on? It goes past the target 4.

parts.title: Remove the extra block
parts.prompt: Cross out ONE block so Bit lands exactly on 4. Which block did you remove? Run it again — what number now?

parts.title: You try — remove to fix
parts.prompt: Run Program 2 from 0. It lands on 0, not 1. Cross out ONE block so Bit lands on 1. Which block did you remove, and where does Bit land?

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: If a program goes too far, it may have an extra block. Take out the one extra step so Bit lands right on the target.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students fix a bug where a program overshoots the target because it has one extra block; they remove the extra step and run again to confirm. Altering existing code by deleting a step and describing how it fixes the outcome is C3.2.

parts.title: Ontario curriculum (Grade 1 — C3 Coding)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: a floor number path 0-5 so students walk past the target and feel the extra step.

parts.title: Run it (about 20 min)
text: 1. I DO: run Program 1 — 'start 1, forward 2 to 3, forward 1 to 4… forward 1 to 5. We passed the target — there's an extra block.'
2. WE DO: Exercise 1 — Bit lands on 5. Exercise 2 — cross out one 'forward 1'; the program lands on 4.
3. YOU DO: Exercise 3 — Program 2 lands on 0; remove one 'back 1' so 0 → 2 → 1.
4. Connect: 'Going too far can mean one extra block — take it out and check.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — Program 1: 1 → 3 → 4 → 5. Bit lands on 5, past the target 4.
Ex 2 — remove one 'forward 1': 1 → 3 → 4. Bit lands on 4.
Ex 3 — Program 2: 0 → forward 2 → 2 → back 1 → 1 → back 1 → 0. Remove one 'back 1': 0 → 2 → 1. Bit lands on 1.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: removing the wrong kind of block — have students count how far past the target Bit went, then remove a step of that size.
Simplify: do Program 1 only; cross out the last block and re-run.
Extend: ask whether removing a different block could also reach the target, and test it.
Success indicator: the child removes one extra block in each program and lands Bit exactly on the target (4, then 1).
